Purpose

This page is the canonical handbook entry for new and existing Redwood employees describing: what it’s like to work at Redwood, our role and career ladder structure, benefits and perks, the high-level hiring and onboarding flow, and a practical guide to the internal tools you’ll use day-to-day. It’s maintained by People Ops; see the reviewers list for cross-functional owners.

----

1) Working at Redwood — culture & expectations

Intro
Redwood is an engineering-first company focused on shipping reliable, high-performance LLM inference for customers. We expect everyone to balance velocity with quality and empathy. Below are the shared expectations and working norms.

Key values and norms
- Customer-focused: prefer decisions that keep customer reliability, security, and cost-efficiency front-of-mind.
- Ownership: teams ship end-to-end and are accountable for live behavior (metrics, incidents, rollouts).
- Iterative excellence: prefer small, reversible changes with measurable metrics.
- Inclusive collaboration: actively solicit feedback, document decisions, and mentor teammates.
- Data-informed: instrument and measure impact of changes; use canary/A-B rollouts where appropriate.

Working model and hours
- Redwood operates a hybrid-friendly model with core collaboration hours 10:00-16:00 PT. Individual schedules are flexible with team alignment required for on-call and customer-facing responsibilities.
- Expected overlap: most teams expect ~4 hours/day overlap with teammates for synchronous work.

Communication channels
- Slack is our primary synchronous channel; #general, team channels, and project channels are used. Use threads to reduce noise.
- Confluence is the canonical place for runbooks, specs, and retrospective documents.
- For long-lived decisions: create an ADR in the relevant architecture-and-standards area and link it from Confluence pages.

----

2) Roles and career ladders

Overview
Redwood maintains leveled career frameworks for engineering, product, design, SRE, and applied ML roles. Each ladder has expectations across four domains: impact, technical skill, collaboration, and leadership. Promotions require demonstrated performance across domains and manager+peer review.

Common role families (high-level)
- Engineering (Backend, Runtime, Platform, Infra, SRE): IC1-IC5, Senior Staff/Principal for system-level leadership.
- Product: Associate PM -> PM -> Senior PM -> Group PM -> Director.
- Applied ML & Evals: Research Engineer/Applied ML Engineer -> Senior -> Staff.
- Design / UX: Designer -> Senior Designer -> Staff Designer -> Design Lead.
- People Ops, Security, Finance, Sales/CS: leveled similarly with role-specific rubrics.

Promotion process (summary)
1. Candidate works with manager to build a promotion packet (examples: goals, outputs, PRs, customer impact metrics, feedback).
2. Manager solicits cross-functional reviewers and completes ladder rubric.
3. People Ops coordinates calibration and final decision; compensation adjustments follow.
4. Timeline: typical cycle aligns to quarterly calibration; off-cycle promotions are possible for clear, sustained impact.

Sample ladder expectations (Engineering IC2 -> IC3)
- Impact: delivers features that ship and reduce manual toil; owns small services or components end-to-end.
- Technical skill: writes maintainable code, has solid debugging skills, and participates in design reviews.
- Collaboration: mentors junior engineers, communicates effectively across teams.
- Leadership: drives small technical initiatives, influences local technical direction.

Career development resources
- Quarterly 1:1 career planning with manager.
- Mentorship program pairing junior and senior engineers.
- Learning stipend ($1,200/year) and curated internal training sessions.

----

3) Benefits & perks (summary)

Benefits overview (high-level)
- Health: comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans with multiple provider options. Redwood covers a portion of premiums for employees and offers dependents coverage.
- Retirement: 401(k) plan with company matching up to 4% after eligibility period.
- Time off: flexible PTO policy, 12 company holidays, 2 company-wide focus weeks, and paid parental leave (16 weeks primary, 8 weeks secondary).
- Financial: competitive salary bands, equity grants, and annual performance bonuses for eligible roles.
- Family & wellness: mental health EAP, fertility support stipend, adoption assistance.

Perks
- Home office stipend for remote-setup ($500 one-time + reimbursement for ergonomic equipment).
- Commuter benefits and monthly transit subsidy where applicable.
- Quarterly team budgets for offsites, team-building, and async social events.
- Free lunches at headquarters on Tuesdays and monthly hackweek lunches.
- Learning stipend (reiterated) and internal speaker series.

How to enroll
- Benefits enrollment is managed through the HR portal (PeoplePortal). New hires receive a benefits packet in their offer email and must enroll within 30 days of start date. People Ops runs benefits Q&A sessions during onboarding week.

----

4) Hiring and onboarding overview

Hiring philosophy
- We hire for technical strength, curiosity, and collaboration. Interview loops focus on problem solving, system design (for senior roles), and cross-functional fit. We evaluate both technical ability and signals of ownership and customer orientation.

New hire hiring loop (high-level)
1. Recruiter screen: assess interest, baseline skills, and compensation alignment.
2. Technical screen (engineers): coding exercise or take-home as applicable.
3. Onsite/loop: 4-5 interviews covering coding, system design, product sense, and culture fit.
4. Debrief and decision within 3 business days after the last interview where possible.

Offer and pre-boarding
- Recruiting team issues offer with clear breakdown: base, equity, target variable (if applicable), start date, and relocation stipend (if offered).
- Pre-boarding tasks: paperwork, benefits enrollment link, and a first-week schedule are shared via PeoplePortal.

Day 0-30 onboarding plan (example)
- Day 0: Welcome email, account provisioning, home-office stipend instructions.
- Week 1: orientation (People Ops), security and compliance training, meet-the-team, dev environment setup, and your first onboarding task (small bug or doc update).
- Weeks 2-4: paired work with a buddy, deeper product and architecture onboarding, first PR and service ownership onboarding, and initial 1:1 with manager to set 30/60/90 goals.

Onboarding owners and checklists
- People Ops: orientation, benefits, cross-org introductions, and HR tasks.
- Hiring manager: technical ramp, role-specific goals, performance expectations.
- Buddy/mentor: day-to-day product and tooling help.
- IT/Security: provisioning, access to cloud accounts, and device enrollment.

----

5) Internal tools guide (quick start)

Accounts and primary tools
- Identity & SSO: Okta (SSO + MFA). First-time login: accept device trust and enroll MFA.
- Code repositories: GitHub Enterprise (org: redwood-inference). Create PRs using the standard template in .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md.
- CI/CD: Buildkite for runtime pipelines; use the pipeline templates in eng-infra/ci-cd-and-build.
- Infrastructure: Terraform in the terraform-and-iac repo; run plan/apply only with reviewer approval and a release ticket.
- Issue tracking: Linear for product and engineering issues; use labels and cycles for planning.
- Documentation: Confluence (this space) for long-form docs and the docs site for end-user docs.
- Slack: primary communication. Teams rely on channel conventions: #eng-runtime, #platform-ops, #product-roadmap. Follow channel naming guidelines in eng-platform/how-tos.
- Observability: Datadog for metrics and dashboards; Sentry for error tracking; access via Okta groups.
- Cost tooling: internal dashboard (CostLens) for token and GPU spend; access gated by role.

Security & compliance notes
- Never store secrets in plain GitHub repositories. Use Vault or the secrets manager specified in cloud-accounts-and-networking.
- Before granting 3rd-party tool access, consult security-and-compliance/security-sdsc checklist.
- For private deployments or customer data, follow the eng-private-deployments/customer-requirements-library guidance.

Day-1 checklist (for engineers)
1. Complete Okta MFA and enroll device.
2. Request GitHub access and add your SSH key.
3. Gain access to Linear and Confluence.
4. Clone dev environment repo; follow README to start local runtime.
5. Join #team channel and schedule first 1:1 with manager.

Common quick commands and snippets
- Git: git checkout -b feat/<ticket-id>-short-desc; git commit -m "<scope>: <summary>"; git push --set-upstream origin feat/<ticket-id>-short-desc
- Buildkite: bk build -g <pipeline-name> --commit <sha>
- Terraform: terraform init; terraform plan -out plan.tf; terraform apply plan.tf (only after reviews and ticket).

Tooling support
- For access issues open a ticket in #it-help or file a request via PeoplePortal > IT Requests.
- For CI/CD failures contact oncall in #platform-ops; include pipeline link and failing step logs.

----

6) Day-to-day operational notes and runbooks

- On-call: engineering teams maintain on-call rotations documented in each team’s runbook (see eng-sre/runbooks and eng-platform/runbooks).
- Incidents: follow the oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process for triage, postmortems, and RCA ownership.
- Rollouts: use canary deployments (5-20% traffic) for infra changes and gate by error budget thresholds.

How to propose changes to the handbook
1. Create a draft Confluence page in this space titled with the proposed change.
2. Add the People Ops reviewer and relevant owners; set status to in_review.
3. After review, update this canonical page with a link to the change and set status to published.

Contacts and escalation
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.com (general questions, benefits, and onboarding issues).
- IT & Access: it-support@redwood.com or Slack #it-help.
- Security: security@redwood.com (report incidents or suspicious access).
